description: We are a team of two students from the Universidad Privada de Trujillo (UPRIT), majoring in Systems Engineering and Artificial Intelligence. Our team consists of Mónica Cahuaza Ramírez and Daniel Isaías Haro Vega. We are passionate about applying systems development, data analysis, and artificial intelligence algorithms to solve complex problems and find innovative solutions to the challenges proposed by NASA.
summary: ECOALERTA PERU is a scientific data analysis platform designed to investigate long-term environmental trends in the Peruvian Amazon. The project uses NASA Earth science data to explore changes in key environmental variables across selected locations in the region. It provides interactive visualizations of historical time series, calculates rates of change using Sen’s slope, and evaluates the statistical significance of trends using the Mann-Kendall test. By transforming complex Earth observation data into accessible scientific insights, ECOALERTA PERU helps users better understand environmental changes and supports evidence-based awareness of the Amazon ecosystem. The project addresses the challenge by combining regional data exploration, time-series visualization, and statistical trend analysis in an accessible digital tool.
details:
Project Details – ECOALERTA PERU

ECOALERTA PERU is a digital platform designed to analyze environmental trends in Peru using NASA Earth observation data. Its main purpose is to transform scientific datasets into accessible visual information that helps users understand environmental changes, particularly in the Peruvian Amazon.

The platform processes historical environmental data, organizes time series, and presents interactive visualizations to identify patterns and long-term changes. It applies statistical methods, including Sen’s slope and the Mann-Kendall test, to estimate trend direction, magnitude, and statistical significance.

The project aims to make Earth science data easier to explore and understand, encouraging environmental awareness and supporting evidence-based decision-making.

Technology and tools: Python, Streamlit, NASA Earth science datasets, Pandas, NumPy, data visualization libraries, and statistical analysis methods.

Innovation and creativity: ECOALERTA PERU combines regional environmental analysis with an accessible interactive interface, connecting scientific data with local environmental challenges.

Expected impact: The project seeks to improve access to environmental information, support understanding of long-term changes in the Peruvian Amazon, and demonstrate how NASA Earth science data can be used to investigate trends in Earth's systems.
